The '''2004 Football Association Community Shield'''  (also known as '''The FA Community Shield in partnership with [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 82nd staging of the [[FA Community Shield]], an annual football match contested by the reigning champions of the [[Premier League]] and the holders of the [[FA Cup]]. It was contested on 8 August 2004 by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], champions of the [[2003–04 FA Premier League|2003–04 Premier League]], and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], who beat [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] in the [[2004 FA Cup Final|final]] of the [[2003–04 FA Cup]]. Watched by a crowd of 63,317 at the [[Millennium Stadium]], Arsenal won the match 3–1.

This was Manchester United's 23rd Community Shield appearance and Arsenal's 18th. Manchester United were without seven of their first-choice players for the game, which meant [[David Bellion]] and [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]] came into the starting 11. [[Cesc Fàbregas]] started alongside [[Gilberto Silva]] in midfield for Arsenal as captain [[Patrick Vieira]] was absent. After a goalless first half, Arsenal took the lead when Gilberto scored in the 50th minute. Striker [[Alan Smith (footballer, born 1980)|Alan Smith]] equalised for Manchester United soon after, but [[José Antonio Reyes]] put Arsenal back in front after United's defenders failed to clear the ball. [[Mikaël Silvestre]] scored an own goal 11 minutes before the end that ensured Arsenal's victory.

Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] was complimentary of his opponents afterwards and was pleased there were no new injuries to report. Opposing manager [[Arsène Wenger]] praised Fàbregas's performance and reiterated his desire to keep Vieira at Arsenal, after speculation regarding the player's impending transfer to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]].

==Background==
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913, it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=[[The Times]]  |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |title=The Shield: From the beginning |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |publisher=Manchester City F.C |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=21 April 2014 }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=3 July 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] acted as the host of the Shield from 1974.<ref name="faru">{{cite web|title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=3 July 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609184712/http://www.thefa.com/fa-community-shield/more/history |archive-date=9 June 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> Cardiff's [[Millennium Stadium]] was hosting the Shield for the fourth time; it took over as the venue for the event while [[Wembley Stadium]] underwent a six-year renovation between 2001 and 2006.<ref name="faru"/>

[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] qualified for the 2004 FA Community Shield as winners of the Premier League.<ref name="hww">{{cite news |title=Multichannel choice; FA Community Shield |page=37 |first=John |last=McNamara |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=7 August 2004}}</ref> They finished their league campaign without a single defeat and earned the nickname "[[The Invincibles (football)|The Invincibles]]", akin to the [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] team that went unbeaten in the inaugural [[Football League]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Articles/Article/2024 |title=1893–1896: Liverpool rocking between 2nd and 1st division |publisher=LFC History |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Media praise for "Invincibles" |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/3718989.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 May 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> The other Community Shield place went to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] who had defeated [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] 3–0 in the [[2004 FA Cup Final]].<ref name="hww"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd win FA Cup |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/3725063.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 May 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> This was the sixth meeting between the two clubs in the Community Shield; Arsenal had won three of those previous meetings to Manchester United's two.<ref>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |publisher=Rec. Sport. Soccer Statistics Foundation |date=15 August 2013 |access-date=11 January 2014}}</ref>

Meetings between Manchester United and Arsenal were often eventful encounters, as both clubs vied for domestic honours.<ref>{{cite news |first1=Simon |last1=Rice |first2=Jack |last2=De Menezes |title=Arsenal v Manchester United: A rivalry like no other |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/arsenal-v-manchester-united-a-rivalry-like-no-other-1676014.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/arsenal-v-manchester-united-a-rivalry-like-no-other-1676014.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=12 February 2014 |access-date=27 June 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref> A goalless draw between the two clubs in September 2003, in which [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]] missed a penalty in [[Association football#Duration and tie-breaking methods|stoppage time]], resulted in [[Battle of Old Trafford|an altercation between both teams]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Deadlock at Old Trafford |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3084372.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 September 2003 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> Several Arsenal players were charged and fined accordingly by [[The Football Association]] (FA) for instigating the brawl; the club was later fined £175,000, the largest ever given to a club by the FA.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3128290.stm |title=Eight charged after bust-up |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 September 2003 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/3228349.stm |title=Arsenal players banned |publisher=BBC Sport |date=30 October 2003 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>

==Pre-match==
[[File:Ronaldo - Manchester_United vs Chelsea.jpg|thumb|[[Cristiano Ronaldo]] was an absentee for Manchester United, due to his commitments for [[Portugal at the 2004 Summer Olympics|Portugal at the Olympics]].]]
Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] said in his press conference: "The game will be competitive. Prestige comes into it, pride comes into it, so it is always competitive when we play Arsenal."<ref>{{cite news |title=Gunners gaffer is in a Vieira bad spot |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3a+Gunners+gaffer+is+in+a+Vieira+bad+spot%3b+Arsenal+v+Man+Utd.-a0120307058 |first=Carl |last=Askew |newspaper=Daily Record |location=Glasgow |date=7 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> He wanted to use the game as a means of preparing his team for their [[UEFA Champions League]] [[2004–05 UEFA Champions League#Third qualifying round|third qualifying round]] game against [[FC Dinamo București|Dinamo București]] the following Wednesday.<ref name="prt">{{cite news |title=Wenger plays games and tiresome Vieira charade rolls on |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/wenger-plays-games-and-tiresome-vieira-charade-rolls-on-d9j0b08ct0v |first=Russell |last=Kempson |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=7 August 2004}} {{subscription required}}</ref> Ferguson was concerned about the state of his squad, with several first team players injured. He was irked that senior players [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and new signing [[Gabriel Heinze]] were absent, on duty for their respective national teams at the [[2004 Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]]: "Apparently, it's supposed to be for amateurs, and money earned is put in trust, but we will be paying their wages while they are away so I don't know what that's all about."<ref name="prev">{{cite news |first1=David |last1=Wilson |first2=Arindam |last2=Rej |title=Hostilities resume for the Community |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/aug/08/newsstory.sport3 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=8 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>

When asked about Arsenal's unbeaten run and whether it would be repeated in English football, Ferguson replied: {{blockquote|"That was a one-off. Arsenal accumulated most points last season so they won the title fairly enough, but they didn't display championship form. They had too many draws. I think they came to a point around January where they realised they could go through the season undefeated, and that was a great driving force for them, but they had to stay undefeated to compensate for the number of draws. It was still an incredible achievement, though."<ref name="prev"/>}}

Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] responded by saying: "Everybody has the freedom to make a judgement. In the last 20 minutes of every game last season, we were never behind. That means we had already done the job before."<ref name="prev"/> He insisted the draws did not reflect on his team's negative tactics, but "because of other teams coming back into the game".<ref name="prev"/> On the issue of [[Patrick Vieira]]'s anticipated move to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], Wenger told reporters the player would remain at Arsenal.<ref name="prt"/> Wenger acknowledged his team were short on experience as a result of selling players and missing Vieira, [[Sol Campbell]] and [[Thierry Henry]], who all were injured. He considered this to be a disadvantage, but argued "...the younger ones have to be given a chance. They all have to take some responsibility."<ref name="prt"/>

Tickets for the game went on general sale on 28 July 2004. They were advertised on the FA website at a cost of between £15 and £40.<ref>{{cite web |title=Shield tickets on sale |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/Tickets_GeneralSale.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20040805001352/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/Tickets_GeneralSale.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 August 2004 |publisher=The Football Association |date=28 July 2004 |access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref> [[Geoff Hurst|Sir Geoff Hurst]] was named as the event's chief guest.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hurst's guest appearance |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/SirGeoffHurst.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20040817085303/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/SirGeoffHurst.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 August 2004 |publisher=The Football Association |date=7 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>

==Match==
===Team selection===
For Arsenal, Thierry Henry was declared fit to start and played alongside [[Dennis Bergkamp]] up front. 17-year-old [[Cesc Fàbregas]] partnered [[Gilberto Silva]] in central midfield, with [[José Antonio Reyes]] and [[Jermaine Pennant]] providing width on either side.<ref name="clock">{{cite news |title=Clockwatch: Arsenal 3–1 Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/3544736.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 August 2004 |access-date=22 March 2011}}</ref> Manchester United were without seven of their first-team players,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2384160/Vintage-red-not-to-Fergusons-taste.html |title=Vintage red not to Ferguson's taste |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |first=Louise |last=Taylor |date=8 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> including Ruud van Nistelrooy, who required surgery on his hernia.<ref>{{cite news |title=Van Nistelrooy injury blow |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/3540500.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=5 August 2004 |access-date=28 June 2014}}</ref> [[Wes Brown]] and [[Louis Saha]] were also ruled out because of injury, so [[David Bellion]] and [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]] came into the first team.<ref name="clock"/>

===Summary===
Arsenal kicked off the match and within the first two minutes forced Manchester United defender [[Gary Neville]] to concede a throw-in.<ref name="clock"/> In the fifth minute, Manchester United won a free kick, but nothing came out of it as [[José Antonio Reyes]] blocked [[Paul Scholes]]'s shot.<ref name="clock"/> Good play by Reyes and Henry fashioned a chance for Bergkamp in the ninth minute, but his strike was off target. Two minutes later a shot by Bergkamp from outside the box was saved by Manchester United goalkeeper [[Tim Howard]].<ref name="clock"/> Before Henry was about to take a corner for Arsenal in the 16th minute, a cigarette lighter was thrown at him from the section occupied by Manchester United supporters – this resulted in police making two arrests during the game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/wales/south_east/3546060.stm |title=Arrests during Community Shield |date=8 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014 |work=BBC News}} See also [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Rorhw4X78s YouTube] footage of incident.</ref> [[Quinton Fortune]] used his pace to get the better of [[Lauren (Cameroonian footballer)|Lauren]], but his cross into the Arsenal penalty area was cleared by [[Pascal Cygan]].<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal continued to threaten – Henry's free kick prompted Howard to make a save and tip the ball over the crossbar, and Bergkamp came close to scoring in the 27th minute after clever play to lose his marker [[John O'Shea]].<ref name="gure">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/aug/09/match.sport14 |title=Arsenal leave United with holes to fill and a score to settle |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |first=Kevin |last=McCarra |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> The football continued to move from one end to the other, with Giggs and Reyes causing problems for their respective defences.<ref name="clock"/> In stoppage time at the end of the first half, Henry had his shot saved by Howard, while Scholes was similarly denied by Arsenal goalkeeper [[Jens Lehmann]].<ref name="clock"/>

{{ external media
| float = left
| topic = 2004 FA Community Shield
| width = 215px
| image1 = {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20040817102404/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/CS_MatchGallery.htm|title=Picture gallary}} via The Football Association website
| image2 = [https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/photo_galleries/3546634.stm Pictures of the match] via BBC Sport
}}

Manchester United made a slight change before the second half commenced, with Neville and O'Shea switching positions, while Arsenal brought [[Robin van Persie]] on in place of Henry.<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal began the half more strongly – Reyes sprinted past the Manchester United defence and went past Howard in the 48th minute, but his shot hit the side-netting.<ref name="clock"/> A minute later Arsenal scored. Bergkamp's pass put Reyes clear to run down the right-hand side of the pitch. He squared the ball to Gilberto, who side-footed it into the empty goal net.<ref name="tele">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2384307/Arsenal-show-there-is-life-beyond-Vieira.html |title=Arsenal show there is life beyond Vieira |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |first=Henry |last=Winter |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> Manchester United responded by making three substitutions – Fortune, Giggs and [[Roy Keane]] off for [[Phil Neville]], [[Diego Forlán]] and [[Darren Fletcher]].<ref name="clock"/> Five minutes after going behind, [[Alan Smith (footballer, born 1980)|Alan Smith]] equalised for Manchester United. A mistake in the Arsenal defence presented him with the chance to hit a half-volley; the ball dipped over Lehmann in goal.<ref name="gure"/> Arsenal retook the lead in the 59th minute – a disjointed move that ended with Reyes shooting the ball low in the bottom left hand corner.<ref name="tele"/> Phil Neville was shown the game's first yellow card in the 62nd minute, after fouling Reyes.<ref name="clock"/> Van Persie's free kick a minute later was deflected for a corner, which came to nothing. [[Jérémie Aliadière]] who came on for Bergkamp sustained a knee injury and had to come off after only a few minutes on the field.<ref name="clock"/> He was replaced by [[Gaël Clichy]], whose arrival according to journalist [[Henry Winter]] "...accelerated Arsenal's drive further, particularly down the left where he kept combining well with Ashley Cole."<ref name="tele"/> In the 72nd minute, [[Eric Djemba-Djemba]] and Cole were each shown a yellow card for clashing with one another.<ref name="clock"/> Arsenal scored their third goal of the match 11 minutes before the end. Cole carried the ball into United's penalty box and his attempted cross hit defender [[Mikaël Silvestre]], who was helpless to prevent the ball going into his own net.<ref name="tele"/>

==Post-match and aftermath==
{{Quote box |width=245px |bgcolor=#FFFFF0 |salign=left |quote="He's a complete player, but there is more to come from him. Ideally you would want to give him one more year [to develop]."|source=[[Arsène Wenger]] on [[Cesc Fàbregas]]'s performance.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal aim for rollover |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/arsenal-aim-for-rollover-dkg9f3b8v2n?region=global |first=Matt |last=Dickinson |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}} {{subscription required}}</ref>}}
Wenger clarified Vieira's future after the match: "My intention is clear: to keep him [...] The challenge in front of us is hugely difficult and we need a complete focus. I'm not resigned to let the story go on. It has all to be sorted out before the season."<ref name="vil">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/aug/09/newsstory.sport12 |title=Wenger sets new D-Day for Vieira |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |first=Matt |last=Scott |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> He added that if Vieira chose to leave, the club could sufficiently replace him: "We've worked very hard in the last five years to get good young players in and you saw that today."<ref name="vil"/> Reyes, who was named man of the match, was frustrated at his missed chance early in the second half, but continued: "I set one up and then scored myself so I was much happier."<ref name="rey"/> Bergkamp was impressed with Fàbregas's performance in the match: "Normally at 17, you might be a bit unsure when you step out. But with players like Cesc, the way he has developed in one year is quite amazing."<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal will stay on top |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3A+Arsenal+will+stay+on+top..+it%27s+child%27s+play+says+Dennis.-a0120382765 |first=Martin |last=Lipton |newspaper=Daily Mirror |location=London |date=10 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>

Ferguson congratulated Arsenal on their win and said of the game: "It was about trying to make sure everyone was fit for Wednesday. I think we have managed to do that. There are no new injuries so far. Hopefully by tomorrow morning it will be a definite."<ref>{{cite news |title=Ferguson relieved as United are unscathed |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3A+Ferguson+relieved+as+United+are+unscathed.-a0120348439 |first=Jim |last=Van Wijk |newspaper=Liverpool Daily Post |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> He believed it was important to substitute Giggs and Keane early in the second half in order for them to recuperate in time for the Dinamo București game. Scholes, however, "...needed a game, which is why I left him on that bit longer."<ref>{{cite news |title=Fergie's Euro crisis |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Football%3A+FERGIE%27S+EURO+CRISIS%3B+Arsenal+3+Man+Utd+1%3A+Brown+out+of...-a0120342660 |first=David |last=McDonnell |newspaper=Daily Mirror |location=London |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> Ferguson felt Manchester United's preparations to the new season were hampered because of the injuries: "It's got a lot to do with summer football. It's not down to the [[UEFA Euro 2004|European Championship]], but you do wonder why the [[2004 Copa América|Copa América]] can't be at the same time. That harmony is never quite right, from Africa to America to Europe. Something should be done about that."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2384332/Wenger-issues-ultimatum-to-Vieira.html |title=Wenger issues ultimatum to Vieira |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |first=Sam |last=Wallace |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref> Giggs said Manchester United needed to take the positives out of the match and anticipated Arsenal as their main rivals in the league: "[They] know what to do and how to handle the pressure when it comes around."<ref>{{cite web |title=Giggs looking ahead |url=http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/FACS_GiggsReaction.htm |archive-url=https://archive.today/20040817103154/http://www.thefa.com/TheFACup/TheFACommunityShield/NewsAndFeatures/Postings/2004/07/FACS_GiggsReaction.htm |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 August 2004 |publisher=The Football Association |date=9 August 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>

The two clubs next faced each other in a [[Battle of the Buffet|league fixture at Old Trafford]] on 23 October 2004, where Arsenal's unbeaten league run of 49 matches came to an end as Manchester United beat them 2–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=Man Utd 2–0 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/3727552.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2004 |access-date=27 June 2014}}</ref>
